svg.font-family: Segoe UI, Inter, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: WDAC MULTI-POLICY GPO DEPLOYMENT
svg.desc: A reference device builds an Audit and an Enforce package from one enforced App Control policy and publishes them to two GPOs in SYSVOL. Both GPOs are linked to the target OU with exactly one link enabled. Windows 11 endpoints in the OU run Deploy-WDACPolicy.ps1 as SYSTEM from the startup script and a recurring scheduled task, verify the SHA-256 hash, and deploy the multiple-policy {GUID}.cip with CiTool only when the version is higher. Win32_DeviceGuard then reports the two DISA STIG values: V-243450 kernel mode and V-243451 user mode, where 0 is OFF, 1 is AUDIT and 2 is ENFORCING.
svg.text: APP CONTROL FOR BUSINESS · AUDIT + ENFORCE GPOs · ONE ENABLED LINK · {GUID}.cip VIA CiTool · NEVER DOWNGRADE
the reference device builds · SYSVOL carries · endpoints deploy themselves as SYSTEM

g.text: CRITICAL · NOT THE BUILT-IN GP SETTING
'Deploy App Control for Business' only writes a single-policy SiPolicy.p7b. A
multiple-policy {GUID}.cip needs CiTool, so each GPO runs a script.
BOTH LINKED TO THE TARGET OU · DISABLE BEFORE ENABLE
IN THE TARGET OU · RUN AS SYSTEM
Deploy the policy themselves, at every boot and on a schedule
GPO startup script · every boot, before logon
GPP task · at creation (+1 min), then every 4 h
Checks the SHA-256 in manifest.json first
Deploys only a HIGHER version · CiTool --update-policy
Never downgrades · never removes · no reboot
Reads Win32_DeviceGuard · WARN 2004 if UMCI is not as expected
Manual run asks Y/N before deploying; no console + no -NoConfirm =

text.font-family: Cascadia Mono, Consolas, Courier New, monospace

g.text: 7_DISA_STIG_CHECK.ps1 prints each value as 0 OFF / 1 AUDIT / 2 ENFORCING
and names the policy, version and GUID in effect.
WIN 11 ENTERPRISE 22H2+ · SERVERS AND DCs SKIPPED

svg.text: TargetOU in GPO-Settings.psd1 · default: the reference device's OU
Both GPOs linked · exactly one link enabled · computer policy refresh every 90-120 min, at boot, or gpupdate /force · security filtering: Authenticated Users
what each mode produces · how to change it safely
Microsoft Windows PAW STIG · App Control
Win32_DeviceGuard 0 = OFF · 1 = AUDIT · 2 = ENFORCING · only 2 passes

g.text: STIG ID WPAW-00-001050 · CAT II · KERNEL MODE
Drivers and kernel code. Windows' own policies already enforce it.
Reads 2 in Audit mode AND in Enforce mode
STIG ID WPAW-00-001060 · CAT II · USER MODE (UMCI)
Apps, DLLs, installers. Needs option 0 (UMCI) ON and option 3 (Audit Mode) OFF.
Audit N · Enforce N+1 · same policy GUID
N restarts at 1 each day; never below the highest known version
Known = source XML · active policy · packages · both GPOs
Audit → Enforce: switch the links only (Enforce is already higher)
Enforce → Audit: switch FIRST, then 1 + 2 (a new, higher pair)
Until then devices log 2001: newer version active, no downgrade
4: AD/SYSVOL versions, hashes, CSEs, links, Audit < Enforce
5: applied GPO, task, active version = package, 3099, STIG
Results: PASS / WARN / FAIL to CSV + transcript in GPO\Logs
DisableLinks: OU → mode None; devices KEEP their policy
RemovePolicy: CiTool --remove-policy (refused while a link is on)
RemoveGpos: unlink and delete both GPOs
